newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran MPs approve outline of $108 billion budget.
newsitem.headline: Iran MPs approve outline of $108 billion budget.

text.p: Iran's parliament on Monday approved a ceiling of 188.7 trillion rials ($107.8 billion) for the budget in the Iranian year starting on March 21, some 38 percent higher than the current year's.

In a parliamentary session broadcast live on Tehran radio, deputies blocked proposals to raise the budgeted oil price by a further 50 cents a barrel above the $17.50 agreed by the government and a parliamentary commission.
The current year's budget of about 137 trillion rials is based on a price of $15.50 per barrel of oil -- Iran's main source of hard cash.
High oil prices have brought Iran $2.67 billion in surplus oil revenue in the first nine months of the current Iranian year, a senior Iranian official said on Monday.
The budget ceiling of 188.7 trillion rials approved on Monday is 551 billion rials, or 0.3 percent, higher than the government budget draft.
Some deputies criticised "hidden deficits" in the budget, saying some projected revenues such as 2.3 trillion rials from state bonds and 2.5 trillion rials in taxes were overoptimistic.
MPs supporting the budget said it would lower inflation, officially put at about 25 percent annually, but critics argued that increases in state spending would fuel inflation.
Parliament will discuss the budget bill in detail for final approval in the coming weeks.
Before taking effect, the budget must be approved by the clergy-based Guardian Council which vets laws passed by parliament for conformity with Islam and the constitution.
